# 1 Maccabees Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_004_page_001.jpg

---

1. Gorgias took five thousand infantry and a thousand elite cavalry and led the force out by night
2. to strike the Judean camp without warning, guided by soldiers from the citadel who knew the terrain.
3. But Judas had gotten word. He led his own fighters toward the royal camp at Emmaus
4. while Gorgias and his force were still away in the dark.
5. Gorgias reached Judas's camp in the middle of the night and found it empty. He headed into the hills, thinking: "They're running from us."
6. At first light Judas appeared on the plain with three thousand men — poorly equipped, without the armor and weapons they needed.
7. What they saw ahead of them was formidable: the Gentile camp, well-built and well-defended, cavalry ringing the perimeter, trained soldiers throughout.
8. Judas spoke to them: "Don't look at their numbers. Don't flinch at their assault.
9. Remember how our ancestors escaped at the Red Sea while Pharaoh's whole army was behind them.
10. Cry out to Heaven now. Maybe he will be merciful. Maybe he will remember the covenant of our fathers and crush this army in front of us today —
11. and every nation on earth will know that someone redeems and saves Israel."
12. The foreigners looked up and saw the Judeans coming for them.
13. They poured out of their camp into battle formation. Judas's men blew the trumpet.
14. The lines crashed together. The Gentiles broke and ran for the plain.
15. The stragglers were cut down from behind. The pursuit went all the way to Gazara, across the plains of Idumea, Azotus, and Jamnia. Three thousand of them died.
16. Judas pulled his men back from the chase.
17. He told them: "Don't go for the plunder yet. The battle's not over.
18. Gorgias and his force are up in the hills — right there. Hold your position, engage the enemy, fight — then take everything you want when it's done."
19. He was still talking when a column came over the ridge from the hills.
20. They saw it immediately: their camp was burning, the smoke rising and telling the story at a distance. Their men had been smashed.
21. The sight of it broke them. Then they looked down at Judas's battle line in the plain — formed up and ready.
22. They broke for Philistine country at a run.
23. Judas brought his men back to loot the camp. They hauled out gold and silver, blue and purple cloth, enormous wealth.
24. On the way back they sang hymns and blessed Heaven — "for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever."
25. Israel had won a great victory that day.
26. The survivors found their way back to Lysias and reported everything.
27. When he heard it, he went pale. He was rattled. Israel hadn't broken the way he had expected. The king's orders had come to nothing.
28. The next year he assembled sixty thousand picked infantry and five thousand cavalry for another campaign against Judah.
29. They marched into Idumea and set up camp at Beth-zur. Judas came out to meet them with ten thousand men.
30. He looked at the army and prayed: "Blessed are you, Savior of Israel — you who broke the assault of the war-hero by the hand of your servant David, and handed the camp of the Philistines over to Jonathan son of Saul and his armor-bearer.
31. Trap this army in the hands of your people Israel. Let them be shamed — cavalry, infantry, the lot.
32. Break their nerve. Melt their confidence. Make them shake with dread of their own coming end.
33. Strike them down with the swords of those who love you, and let everyone who knows your name sing praises."
34. The battle began. About five thousand of Lysias's men fell in the fighting before them.
35. Lysias saw his soldiers in rout. He saw the fire in Judas's men — the way they were prepared to live or die with honor. He pulled back to Antioch and started hiring mercenaries, planning to return to Judah with a bigger army next time.
36. Judas and his brothers conferred: "Our enemies are broken. Let's go up and purify the sanctuary and rededicate it."
37. The entire army came together and marched up to Mount Zion.
38. What they found there devastated them. The sanctuary was a ruin. The altar had been desecrated. The gates were burned to ash. Weeds had overrun the courts like a forest, like a wild hillside. The priests' chambers were collapsed.
39. They tore their clothes. They wept loudly. They poured ashes on their heads.
40. They threw themselves face-down on the ground. They blew the signal trumpets. They cried out to Heaven.
41. Judas assigned troops to hold off the men in the citadel while he set about purifying the sanctuary.
42. He selected priests — men of integrity, devoted to the Torah.
43. They cleaned the sanctuary and hauled the defiled stones out to an unclean place outside the city.
44. They debated what to do with the altar of burnt offerings. It had been desecrated, fouled by the Gentiles.
45. The right answer was clear: tear it down. It could not stand — it was a shame and a reproach. So they tore it down.
46. They stored the stones in a fitting place on the temple mount, to wait until a prophet came who could give them a definitive word about what to do with them.
47. They took uncut stones, as the Torah commands, and built a new altar exactly like the old one.
48. They rebuilt the sanctuary and the interior of the temple and the courts.
49. They made new sacred vessels — lampstand, incense altar, table — and brought them inside.
50. They lit the incense on the altar. They kindled the lamps on the lampstand. Light filled the temple.
51. They set the bread of the Presence on the table. They hung the curtains. Every task was finished.
52. On the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month — the month of Chislev — in the one hundred and forty-eighth year, they rose at dawn
53. and offered sacrifice on the new altar of burnt offerings, exactly as the Torah required.
54. The very day, the very date on which the Gentiles had desecrated it — on that same day it was rededicated with songs and harps and lutes and cymbals.
55. The whole people fell on their faces. They worshiped. They blessed Heaven, who had brought them to this moment.
56. For eight days they celebrated the dedication of the altar — burnt offerings rising day after day, offerings of well-being and thanks, joy filling the air.
57. They decorated the front of the temple with golden crowns and shields. They rebuilt the gates and the priests' chambers and hung new doors.
58. Joy spread through all the people like a wave. The contempt of the Gentiles had been wiped away.
59. Judas and his brothers and the whole congregation of Israel made a binding decree: the days of the rededication of the altar were to be celebrated with joy and gladness every year for eight days, beginning on the twenty-fifth of Chislev — year after year, without end.
60. In those same days they built high walls and strong towers around Mount Zion to keep the Gentiles from marching in and trampling it again.
61. He posted a garrison to hold the place, then fortified Beth-zur as well, so the people would have a stronghold guarding the Idumean border.
